scope: Static timing-boundary investigation; not a performance subtraction
findings: Original Session::DecodeStep prepares sampling, forwards one token with host logits, and finishes state bookkeeping. The final true argument is stop_at_eos, not materialize.
Original SamplerState::SampleGreedy scans once and tests finiteness when a new maximum is selected; isolated nonfinite values are skipped.
Corrected diagnostic Argmax retains a complete finite scan followed by std::max_element, rejecting every nonfinite value. Timed work therefore still differs from original production sampling.
Both fresh Q2/UD benchmark arms use the same stricter Argmax and matched completed-work scope. A lower diagnostic UD rate cannot replace the historical production target.
No sampler or production engine implementation is changed in this campaign.
next: Measure strict single-pass argmax separately or use a pinned production Session/Sampler comparison for absolute baseline reproduction; never remove finite checks just to raise reported throughput.
